The 'absent directory' tests were updated to establish a project first — the intent (directory absent → []) is preserved, but the project itself must exist.

AC6: All 2330 tests pass (79 test files).
Edge case 1 — repoName path traversal: caught inside resolveProjectStore's own assertSafeSlug(repoName) call (gui/api.ts:172). Defense is present.

comments.note: Behavioral change flagged by Developer: handleListDialogues and handleListChunks now return NOT_FOUND when the project does not exist (resolveProjectStore throws) instead of silently returning []. This is correct behavior but is a semantic change that the Reviewer should note — callers that previously relied on [] for missing projects may need updates.

In handleGetDialogueFile and handleGetChunkFile, assertSafeSlug runs first, then the filename allowlist regex, then resolveProjectStore. The ordering is deliberate (fail fast on bad slug/filename before incurring I/O). The pattern is consistent and correct.

Edge case: repoName with path-traversal content (e.g. '../etc') is caught inside resolveProjectStore via its own assertSafeSlug(repoName) call — not in the handler-level guard. Defense is present but layered differently from slug validation. Acceptable.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (mcp-server/gui/api.ts, mcp-server/tests/gui/api.test.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 1 Low (noted). Security sign-off: PASS. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. Path traversal controls are layered and sound; filename allowlists and defence-in-depth prefix checks are correctly applied.

comments.note: A01/A03 — repoName path-traversal validation: repoName is validated inside resolveProjectStore() via assertSafeSlug(repoName) rather than at the handler call site. This is a valid security layering choice (the guard runs before any path construction), but the defence-in-depth note from QA (ledger-root.ts also validates each segment independently inside resolveProjectDir) confirms multiple independent barriers are present. No vulnerability — Low for awareness.

No security findings for the assertSafeSegment refactor. assertSafeSegment() in path-validator.ts uses the same SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) that was previously used inline. The Boolean(segment) guard is retained as defence-in-depth for empty-string rejection. Semantic equivalence confirmed — no regression in security guarantees.

A03 — Filename allowlists: DIALOGUE_FILENAME_RE (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.md$/) and CHUNK_FILENAME_RE (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.jsonl$/) both enforce strict allowlist patterns before any filesystem access. A secondary resolve()+startsWith(dir+sep) prefix check is present in handleGetDialogueFile and handleGetChunkFile as defence-in-depth. Both guards are correctly ordered (allowlist first, I/O second).

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/api.ts and mcp-server/tests/gui/api.test.ts.

All four handlers (handleListDialogues, handleGetDialogueFile, handleListChunks, handleGetChunkFile) correctly call assertSafeSlug(slug) first, then resolveProjectStore(ledgerRoot, slug, repoName), and construct subdirectory paths via join(store.storageDir, DIR).
SAFE_SLUG_REGEX fully removed from gui/api.ts imports. assertSafeSlug now delegates to assertSafeSegment() throughout the module.

resolveProjectStore correctly validates repoName via assertSafeSlug(repoName) before constructing the qualified {repo}/{slug} path. AMBIGUOUS→NOT_FOUND downgrade is correctly documented as a security invariant.
handleRenameProject uses assertSafeSegment(newSlug) directly with validationError() — semantically correct (invalid proposed slug is a validation error, not NOT_FOUND). No change needed.
Behavioral change for missing projects (NOT_FOUND instead of [] from handleListDialogues/handleListChunks) is semantically correct and intentional.
No Blocking issues. No Fix-Forward changes applied.

comments.note: handleRenameProject uses assertSafeSegment(newSlug) directly (boolean predicate) rather than the throwing assertSafeSlug wrapper, then calls validationError(). This distinction is semantically correct — an invalid proposed new slug is a validation error, not a NOT_FOUND. The inconsistency is intentional and appropriate. No change needed.

The behavioral change in handleListDialogues and handleListChunks — returning NOT_FOUND (not []) when the project does not exist — is the more semantically correct behavior. The old behavior (silently returning [] for a non-existent project slug) masked configuration errors. Any callers that relied on the empty-array response for missing projects must be updated.

[documentation-forward] The AMBIGUOUS → NOT_FOUND downgrade in resolveProjectStore() (api.ts line ~183) is a security-critical design decision preventing cross-namespace existence leaks. It is documented only in an inline comment. The api-surface.md should capture this invariant explicitly so future maintainers know not to restore the AMBIGUOUS message path without a security review.

[documentation-forward] The api-surface.md should document the distinction between assertSafeSegment() (boolean predicate, used when the calling site constructs its own error type) and assertSafeSlug() (throwing guard, used at handler entry points). handleRenameProject demonstrates the canonical pattern for using assertSafeSegment() with validationError() — this pattern is not currently documented in the manifest.
